instruction: Set titles in slides 3 and 4 to green (#00FF00) and increase their size to 80 pt.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing title color to green (#00FF00) and size to 80pt in slides 3 and 4. Evaluator extracts both color and size properties and gives partial credit (0.5 per property per slide).
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 1.0 = Both titles have correct color AND size, 0.75 = Both have one property correct, 0.5 = One title fully correct or both partially correct, 0.25 = Minimal progress, 0.0 = No changes
metadata.verification: Verified by analyzing actual PowerPoint file structure: file contains 6 slides with titles in Gloria Hallelujah and Poppins fonts. Target slides identified based on slide indices.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter uses unreliable heuristic to identify title: finds shape with largest font size instead of using slide.shapes.title
This heuristic may fail if body text or other elements have larger fonts than the title, causing wrong shape to be identified
If wrong shape is identified, evaluator will check wrong text properties, leading to false negatives or false positives

All other aspects are correct: slide indices properly mapped (slides 3,4 human = indices 2,3), metric logic sound with proper partial credit, postconfig adequate (saves file), expected values correct, complete coverage of both color and size requirements
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Replace title identification heuristic in getter (lines 38-52 in pptx_titles.py) with: if slide.shapes.title exists, use it directly; only fallback to largest-font heuristic if no title shape exists
Add validation to ensure identified shape is actually title-like (e.g., positioned in typical title area, shorter text length)
Add logging/warning when fallback heuristic is used to help debug verification failures
